meta.title: Pantheus — Software designed around the way you operate
meta.description: Pantheus builds software around each business's real workflow, then packages what works into products: Pantheus Office for office teams and Pantheus Production for factories.

hero.title: Your business is <acc>one of a kind</acc>. Your software should be too.
hero.lead: Pantheus builds software around the way each business actually runs — then packages what works into products. Built with AI, improved on weekly feedback.

office.desc: Tasks, projects, meetings, documents and chat — one flow for the whole office day.

production.desc: ERP for the factory floor: bills of materials, planning, purchasing, inventory, production orders and finished goods.

problem.title: Big software makes you change how you work. Spreadsheets can't keep up.
problem.quote: “How many units can we build right now?”
problem.body: With spreadsheets, that question takes hours — and the answer is stale by the time it reaches you. With packaged software, you bend your process to fit someone else's screens. Pantheus takes a third path: software drawn from the way your work actually flows.

approach.title: Start tailored. Grow into a product.
approach.group: The three steps of the approach

steps.title: Start from how you actually operate.
steps.body: We follow the real flow of work — from the moment materials arrive at the gate to the moment a document hits the ledger. Every event gets the same six questions: who does it, when, what data, how the status changes, which document, and what the exceptions are.
get: Software that follows your actual workflow
Runs on your infrastructure; your data stays yours
We start with your most expensive bottleneck

steps.d: Feedback today, an update this week
steps.title: A feedback loop measured in days, not quarters.
steps.body: People press “Send feedback” on the screen they're using. We write the spec, AI writes the code, engineers own the architecture and the tests. Change becomes cheap enough to say “yes” more often.
get: A feedback button on every screen
Small, steady updates — no waiting for a “big release”
Changing a process is no longer a six-month project

steps.title: What works becomes a product.
steps.body: What worked well in the first deployments is packaged into Pantheus Office and Pantheus Production. Later customers start from a base that already runs in production — and everything else is still tailored.
get: Faster rollout on a proven base
What's specific to you stays yours

principles.title: What doesn't change, tailored or productized.

items.label: Optimized for you
items.title: Your process is the blueprint.
items.body: We don't force your business to run the software's way. The software is drawn from your needs and the way you operate.

items.label: Runs on your data
items.title: Your data is priceless.
items.body: A dedicated server, designed to run on the factory's local network. You keep full control of your data.

items.label: Outcomes, not features
items.title: Every feature is tied to a number you care about.
items.body: We start from the bottleneck: inventory loss, line stoppages, working capital. If it doesn't move a number, we don't build it.

items.label: Built for operators
items.title: Simple enough for everyone to use.
items.body: Most ERP projects fail at adoption. Guides run on the real screens: minimal training, clean data from day one.

items.label: Built with AI
items.title: Ready to change when you do.
items.body: AI helps us write code faster; engineers own the architecture and the quality. Changing a process is no longer a six-month project.

ai.title: Ask in plain language. Get real answers.
ai.body: AI reads your own operating data — documents, plans, tasks — instead of making you read dashboards. Pan is live in Pantheus Office; asking the factory in plain language is on the Production roadmap.

how.title: Three steps, starting from one bottleneck.

steps.b: Walk the real flow of work, interview every role, and find the most expensive bottleneck.
Deploy a system that solves that bottleneck on top of an existing product, tailoring what's specific to you.
Add workflows as you grow — at your pace and on your terms, not on a vendor's roadmap.

closing.heading: Let's build the system your business deserves.
closing.lead: No templates. No lock-in. We start by coming to see how you operate today.

meta.title: Pantheus Office — One workday, one flow
meta.description: Tasks, projects, meetings, documents, chat and purchase requests in one place, with Pan — an AI assistant.

hero.title: One workday, one <acc>flow</acc>.
hero.lead: Tasks, projects, meetings, documents and chat in one place. Every screen is honed on everyday actions — not for the demo.

stops.title: One office, one flow of work.
stops.desc: Click any area, or follow the route — from switching on in the morning to settling purchase requests at the end of the day.

stops.title: Know what comes first the moment you log in.
stops.desc: The inbox gathers what needs you: overdue work, work due today and tomorrow, and unread notifications.

hots.b: Overdue work comes first, with its project and how many days late. No digging through projects to find what you owe.
Drag a task onto your calendar as a block of time. Scheduling it doesn't change the task's start or due date.

stops.title: Minutes written right on the meeting page.
stops.desc: Take minutes in the same editor as Documents. Duration and attendance are recorded; minutes are searchable like any other document.

hots.b: Headings, lists, tables, images — inserted with slash commands. Type @ to mention a colleague right in the minutes.
Join the video call from the meeting page; attendance is recorded automatically. Meeting in person? Add an offline meeting and still keep minutes.

stops.title: Delivery projects run by phase and sign-off date.
stops.desc: Phases, steps and tasks on one Gantt chart. Sign-off dates sit on the timeline; a day late and the whole team sees it.
specs: Know which phase is slipping, and why

hots.b: Three levels on one Gantt chart, each phase collapsible. The sign-off date is its own milestone, flagged when late.
Delivery by phase for client work, Development on kanban, General for running the business — each with its own view.

stops.title: The description and the AI prompt in one task.
stops.desc: Coding work carries extra fields for developers and a Prompt block for a coding agent. The kanban has a Review column so AI work always passes human eyes.
specs: Assign work to people and AI alike

hots.t: A prompt for the coding agent
hots.b: Write the request once: people can read it, an agent can run it. Paste images, attach files up to 25 MB.
To do, Doing, Review, Done — AI work stops at Review so a person checks it before it's done.

stops.title: Group chat — and ask Pan.
stops.desc: Groups and direct messages sit next to the work. Pan, the AI assistant, lives in the conversation list like a colleague.

hots.b: Ask about your work, projects and documents in Vietnamese or English. Pan also drafts tasks from messages — created only once you confirm.
Quoted replies, reactions, attachments — enough that you don't need another chat app.

stops.title: The team's documents, tagged by topic.
stops.desc: One editor at a time, comments on each paragraph, version history, export to Word and PDF. Topic tags go up to 3 levels deep so you can browse them as a tree.
specs: One home for what the team knows

hots.b: Browse as a tree: /internal, then /internal/product… Tags are paths, not a flat list.
Files from tasks, chat and documents land in one library, with previews for images, PDFs and video.

stops.title: Request, approve, reimburse, settle — no email.
stops.desc: Every request moves through clear stages: awaiting approval, awaiting purchase, awaiting transfer, awaiting settlement, recognized — or sent back for changes.

hots.b: No more “did I send it?” — everyone sees which stage a request is at and who it's waiting on.
Attach the VAT invoice and the proof of transfer right on the request; at least one is required before it can be marked as bought.

meta.title: Pantheus Production — ERP for small and mid-sized factories
meta.description: Bills of materials, planning, purchasing, inventory, production orders and finished goods on one flow of data. Rolling out at an electric vehicle factory.

hero.title: From materials at the gate to finished goods in stock — <acc>one flow of data</acc>.
hero.lead: ERP for small and mid-sized factories in Vietnam: bills of materials, planning, purchasing, inventory, production orders and finished goods. Rolling out at an electric vehicle factory — with new workflows added every week.

facts.v: Rolling out at an EV factory

stops.title: One factory, one flow of data.
stops.desc: The dotted line is the material flow: from the truck at the gate, through the store, onto the line, into a finished product. Every step creates a document — and the software follows exactly those steps.

hots.b: The start-of-day screen: slips awaiting approval, today's orders short on materials, materials to buy. Each tile opens exactly the list to work through.

stops.title: Versioned bills of materials, per colour.
stops.desc: Set up materials, colours and the bill of materials (BOM) for each product. Sub-assemblies like the seat have their own BOM. Every change goes through a draft — the active version is never overwritten.
specs: Material needs right for every colour

hots.b: Edit a draft, activate it when it's ready. Change history is kept; export to Excel any time.
Each colour of a product has its own materials list. A sub-assembly like the seat is a product with a BOM of its own.

stops.title: From weekly output to a list of materials to buy.
stops.desc: Enter the planned output for the week. The system multiplies out the BOM, subtracts stock and incoming deliveries, and shows what needs buying.
specs: A buy list, ready to order

hots.b: Press “Calculate shortfall”: no VLOOKUP, no waiting for someone to sign off the numbers. Raise purchase orders straight from the result.
See how many units current stock can build, and which material is the constraint — before locking in the plan.

stops.title: Orders per supplier, receipts tied to the order.
stops.desc: Split the buy list into one order per supplier. When the truck arrives, the storekeeper creates a goods receipt against the order — the order knows how much has arrived and how much is still due.
specs: Every delivery matched to its order

hots.b: Receive in parts across several receipts; the order shows received against ordered.
Approving an order and receiving it are separate statuses. Receiving has three levels: not received, receiving, fully received — no single “status” column doing everything.

stops.title: Stock is a ledger, not a cell you type into.
stops.desc: Every stock figure is derived from approved receipts, issue slips and stock counts. When numbers drift, count and approve an adjustment — with a trail.
specs: Goods receipt · Issue slip · Stock count

hots.b: Draft, awaiting approval, approved: only approved slips change stock. Approved by mistake? A manager cancels it with a reason, and the system posts a reversing entry.
Create a stock count, enter what was actually counted, approve to adjust stock. Quickly filter materials below minimum or negative.

stops.title: One production order, issue slips generated for you.
stops.desc: Operations creates the day's order; the system calculates materials from the BOM and generates the issue slips. The storekeeper just picks and approves.
specs: The right materials, in full, on time

hots.b: One “Generate issue slip” button: materials and quantities pre-filled from each order line's BOM.
Each order line knows whether its issue slip is draft, awaiting approval or approved — and whether finished goods have been received.

stops.title: Finished goods received from the production order.
stops.desc: Completed products go into stock on a finished goods receipt tied to the order. Finished stock by code and colour, traceable to every receipt.
specs: Know exactly how many vehicles are in stock

hots.b: Stock by code, colour and unit — calculated from approved documents.
Double-click a row to open its stock ledger: every receipt and issue that changed the stock of that code.

stops.title: Warranty looked up by VIN.
stops.desc: Customers or dealers check warranty by VIN; defects are logged by material and supplier. This part is still planned.

hots.b: A public page: enter the VIN and see the warranty end date — no call centre needed.
Group defects by material and supplier, as evidence for returns and supplier choice.

tour.body: Every physical step in the factory creates a document — and the software follows exactly those steps. Click a number to jump to an area, click + for details.
tour.screenNote: The screen below follows the stop you pick above. The data is illustrative; the name and logo are your factory's.

items.b: Walkthroughs by job — production orders and issue slips, planning and purchase orders, stock counts — that run step by step on the screen you're using.
Admins see the system exactly as operations or a storekeeper sees it — support without guesswork.
A “Send feedback” button in the corner. Say it at the moment and in the place you got stuck — and see it fixed in the next loop.
Every slip records who created it, who approved or rejected it, and when. Approved by mistake? A manager cancels it with a reason and the system posts a reversal — nothing is overwritten.
Goods receipts, issue slips and purchase orders print on A4 for signing by hand when your process still needs signatures.
The software carries your factory's name and logo. Pantheus appears only in one “Powered by” line.

deploy.title: A dedicated server for your factory. Your data stays in your hands.

items.b: One database per legal entity. Designed to run on the factory's local network.
Updates are built and tested ahead of time; the server just runs them.
Automatic backups every day, with the last 30 days kept.
Export any list to Excel at any time — your data is never locked inside the software.
If two people edit the same slip, whoever saves second is warned — nothing is silently overwritten.
Use it on desktop and phone through the browser, installable as an app.

roadmap.title: An open roadmap, updated against a real factory.
roadmap.body: Priorities are set by our customers' bottlenecks, not by a feature list.

items.b: Bring the system into daily operation at the first electric vehicle factory, together with the store and operations teams.
Print labels and scan them when finished goods are received; open a vehicle's production order from its VIN.
A public lookup page, warranty slips, and replacement parts deducted straight from stock.
Group defects by material and supplier, as evidence for returns and supplier reviews.
Stock movement by period, output by order, material consumption against the BOM.
Ask in plain language: what do we need to buy this week, which supplier causes the most defects.

closing.heading: Start with your factory's most expensive bottleneck.
closing.lead: One walk along the material flow with your team. Then we propose what to build first, and what can wait.
